observed_original_abi.calling_convention_note: INDETERMINATE, and deliberately left null here. The body is byte-identical under cdecl, stdcall, thiscall and fastcall; the derived record abstains with `abstained_because: ["no_discriminator: no stack-argument read and no positive receiver evidence"]` and records `C10` (byte-identical under all four) at confidence UNKNOWN. The four convention names are kept OUT of the `calling_convention` field on purpose: the index extractor resolves that field to a single token by substring, and a sentence naming all four resolves to whichever it tests first -- which is how a metadata record that asserts nothing ends up asserting the wrong one. RET -- no immediate, so the callee performs zero stack cleanup and there are no callee-popped stack words
no conditional branch anywhere in the body, so the load is unconditional and there is no path that skips it
no call and no jump out of the body
no store: the committed data-reference artifact records exactly one row for this body and it is a READ
ECX is never read, so there is no receiver register
no stack slot is ever read, so there are no ordinary stack arguments

semantic_contract.summary: A two-instruction absolute global-slot accessor. It loads the 32-bit word at fixed address 0x0167eae8 into EAX and returns it, leaving the slot and every other byte of memory untouched.
semantic_contract.preconditions: none. The body reads no stack slot, no register argument and no receiver, so there is nothing a caller must set up. It does NOT test the slot for null and does not default one.
semantic_contract.postconditions: the 4 bytes at 0x0167eae8 are byte-identical before and after. EAX holds their value on return. No other architectural state is modified.
semantic_contract.ownership: the returned pointer is BORROWED. The body takes no reference, stores nothing, and releases nothing, so the pointee's lifetime is entirely the caller's concern.
semantic_contract.thread_safety: not claimed. The slot is a plain global read with no synchronisation in the body; whether callers serialise access is outside this body's evidence.
semantic_contract.idempotence: the entry is a pure function of the slot's current contents and may be called any number of times with the same answer.
semantic_contract.failure_modes: none in the body. If the slot is null the entry returns null: there is no null check, no sentinel and no error path, which is itself an observable property of the two-instruction listing.

semantic_findings: The body is a LOAD, not an address computation. EAX receives the word's value; the LEA-form error is refuted by the model test, which returns the slot's own address as one of its eleven mutants.
The access is segment-absolute (DS:0x0167eae8) through the `a1` moffs32 form: there is no base or index register and therefore no receiver of any kind.
The load is unconditional -- no conditional branch exists in the body -- so there is no path on which the slot is not read.
The read is provably read-only: one data-reference row for this body, mode `read`, and no other reference to the address anywhere in the reference database.
The cleanup is zero bytes on the callee side (bare RET), measured at run time by sampling ESP across the call rather than asserted from the convention spelling.
The word's IDENTITY is unknown. It is modelled as a pointer to an incomplete type because sampled callers dereference it, and nothing further is claimed about it.
unresolved_questions: What class or object does 0x0167eae8 hold? No writer of the slot exists in the current analysis state, so its publication and teardown paths are unlocated. The raw-dword note in reconstruction/metadata/wave13-w1-core-b16/00b515e0.json (the address occurs once in the file, at 0x0073d311, as a decodable `A1 E8 EA 67 01 C3` in a region Ghidra has not split into a function) was NOT re-verified by this worker and is cited only as a lead.
Does 0x0167eae8 ever alias any neighbouring slot (0x0167eae0, 0x0167eae4, 0x0167eaf0, 0x0167eaf8)? Adjacency in the .data tail proves nothing and no writer was located.

Is the returned word a pointer, a handle, or an id? Three sampled callers dereference it at +0x20 or move it into ECX as a receiver, which is why it is modelled as a pointer -- but no callee through it has been resolved and no member is claimed.

Which calling convention do the 90 direct callers actually use? The body cannot discriminate between the four, so the declared __cdecl is a source-side choice and the real answer needs a caller-side or import-side observation.
What is at displacement +0x20 of the pointee? Sampled callers read it; this body never does, so no member name is claimed.
Runtime: no original-process trace exists in this repository for this target, so nothing here is a runtime claim.

classification_rationale: The complete 6-byte body is recovered exactly: both instructions, the encoding and its operand bytes, the absolute address they spell, the absence of any branch, call, store, receiver or stack argument, the read-only access mode, the zero callee cleanup, and the four-byte width of the return are all read directly from the listing and corroborated by the committed data-reference row and the committed xref export. That is well above a bare name. It is not IMPLEMENTED because three material elements are bounded rather than established, and each bound is named: (1) the slot's identity is unknown -- no writer exists in the analysis state and nothing says what it holds; (2) the returned word is modelled as a pointer to an INCOMPLETE type on the strength of three sampled callers, and no callee through it has been resolved and no member claimed; (3) the calling convention is INDETERMINATE -- the body is byte-identical under all four and the derived ABI record abstains, so the declared __cdecl is a source-side choice. No SDK identity is claimed at all: the Spore-ModAPI checkout is absent from this machine, so no SDK-side search was performed.
confidence: HIGH for the mechanics (every one read off the complete listing or a committed artifact); LOW for the slot's identity and for the pointee type, both of which are left unclaimed.
